description: Changing where a vendor gets paid is one of the highest-risk actions an agent can touch: it is the standard business-email-compromise / payment-diversion pattern. This policy encodes the two-step defence. Step one is a verified callback: the change must be confirmed out-of-band with a previously known contact at the vendor (the fixtures record this as verified_callback_completed, supplied by whatever verification workflow ran it — this example does not perform the callback). Without it, the change is denied, not merely queued. Step two is dual approval: with the callback verified, a second human must still approve before the change is applied.
fallback_reason: Verification state was not fully stated; the policy denies by default.

rules.reason: No verified callback to a previously known vendor contact has been completed. Bank-detail changes are never applied on the strength of the request alone.
Callback verified, but the required second approver has not signed off yet.
Verified callback completed and dual approval recorded; the change may be applied.

title: Vendor bank-detail changes — verified callback first, then dual approval
